```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Grevel_2019_sorafenib"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Grevel_2019_sorafenib"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.12634> (open access, PMC6742948)

Grevel 2019 built a population PK model of sorafenib from ten pooled studies
and used its post hoc clearances to derive exposure metrics (AUC12, AUC12AV)
for parametric time-to-event models of progression-free survival and adverse
events in the DECISION trial in radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid
cancer (DTC). This library model is the population PK model. The time-to-event
models are described in the last section; their parameter estimates are not
published, so they are not part of the model.

# Population

The PK analysis pooled 3141 sorafenib concentrations from 859 individuals in
10 phase I-IV studies (Grevel 2019 Results and Table S1): 39 healthy volunteers
given single oral doses with dense sampling in two phase I studies, and
patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC, n = 332), renal cell carcinoma
(RCC, n = 332) and DTC (DECISION, n = 156) given 400 mg twice daily with sparse
sampling. Each DECISION patient contributed one PK sample, drawn after an
unsupervised dose.

Table S2 reports a median (range) age of 62 (21-97) years and body weight of
70 (34-140) kg; 211 of 859 (25 percent) were women (46 percent in DECISION) and
35 percent were Asian. The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Grevel_2019_sorafenib")$population`.

# Source trace

Each `ini()` entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Grevel_2019_sorafenib.R`
carries its source location as an in-file comment. The table collects them.

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| Three transit compartments (shared ktr) into a one-compartment model with linear elimination | n/a | Figure S2 (ODEs for A1-A4); Results, Population PK model |
| CL_i = CL_TV x (1 + theta8 x female) x (1 + theta9 x DECISION) x exp(eta1) | n/a | Figure S2 |
| V_i = V_TV x exp(eta2) | n/a | Figure S2 |
| F1 = 1 (steady state), theta7 (single dose) | n/a | Figure S2 |
| Ct = A4 / V1 x (1 + eps), SD theta4 or theta6 by number of samples on the occasion | n/a | Figure S2 |
| CL/F (theta1) | 9.4 L/h | Table S3; Table 1 (male, HCC/RCC) |
| V1/F (theta2) | 554 L | Table S3 |
| ktr (theta3) | 1.0 1/h | Table S3 |
| F1, phase I single dose (theta7) | 1.9 | Table S3 |
| Female effect on CL/F (theta8) | -0.211 | Table 1 (-21.1 percent); Table S3 prints -0.2 |
| DECISION effect on CL/F (theta9) | -0.506 | Table 1 (-50.6 percent); Table S3 prints -0.5 |
| IIV CL (omega squared) | 0.2 | Table S3 |
| IIV V1 (omega squared) | 0.4 | Table S3 |
| Proportional SD, several samples per occasion (theta4) | 0.3 | Table S3 |
| Additive SD (theta5) | 0 fixed (omitted) | Table S3 |
| Proportional SD, single-sample occasion (theta6) | 0.5 | Table S3 |
| sigma squared | 1 fixed (SDs carried by theta4 / theta6) | Table S3, Figure S2 |

# Virtual cohort

Patient data are not public. Four virtual arms cross sex with study (DECISION
vs the other patient studies), all on the DECISION regimen of 400 mg twice
daily for 35 days, long enough for the slowest arm (female DECISION, half-life
about 105 h) to reach steady state. A fifth arm is a single 400 mg dose in a
male phase I healthy volunteer.

```{r cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190325)

arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,                ~SEXF, ~STUDY_DECISION, ~STUDY_SORAFENIB_PHASE1, ~SAMPLE_INTENSIVE,
  "Male, HCC/RCC",               0L,              0L,                      0L,                0L,
  "Female, HCC/RCC",             1L,              0L,                      0L,                0L,
  "Male, DTC (DECISION)",        0L,              1L,                      0L,                0L,
  "Female, DTC (DECISION)",      1L,              1L,                      0L,                0L
)

tau <- 12
n_doses <- 70L
dose_times <- seq(0, by = tau, length.out = n_doses)
t_last <- max(dose_times)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(
  seq(0, t_last, by = 6),
  seq(t_last, t_last + tau, by = 0.1)
)))

make_events <- function(arm_row, ids, amt, dose_times, obs_times) {
  ev <- rxode2::et(amt = amt, time = dose_times, cmt = "depot") |>
    rxode2::et(time = obs_times, cmt = "central") |>
    as.data.frame()
  ev <- ev[rep(seq_len(nrow(ev)), times = length(ids)), ]
  ev$id <- rep(ids, each = nrow(ev) / length(ids))
  for (nm in setdiff(names(arm_row), "treatment")) ev[[nm]] <- arm_row[[nm]]
  ev$treatment <- arm_row$treatment
  ev
}
```

# Typical-value check against Table 1

Table 1 of Grevel 2019 lists the model's apparent clearance and steady-state
AUC over a 12-hour dosing interval (400 mg twice daily) for each sex in
DECISION and in the HCC/RCC studies. These are typical-value quantities, so
the comparison uses `rxode2::zeroRe()`.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Grevel_2019_sorafenib")
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

ev_typ <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  make_events(arms[i, ], ids = i, amt = 400, dose_times = dose_times, obs_times = obs_times)
}))

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_typ, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r pknca-typical}
run_ss_nca <- function(sim, events, start, tau) {
  conc <- sim |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
  conc <- dplyr::bind_rows(
    conc,
    conc |> dplyr::distinct(id, treatment) |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, Cc = 0)
  ) |>
    dplyr::distinct(id, treatment, time, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time)
  doses <- events |>
    dplyr::filter(evid == 1) |>
    dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)
  intervals <- data.frame(
    start = start, end = start + tau,
    auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, cav = TRUE
  )
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
    PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h"),
    PKNCA::PKNCAdose(doses, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg"),
    intervals = intervals
  ))
}

nca_typ <- run_ss_nca(sim_typ, ev_typ, start = t_last, tau = tau)

table1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,                ~auclast,
  "Male, HCC/RCC",               42.4,
  "Female, HCC/RCC",             53.7,
  "Male, DTC (DECISION)",        85.8,
  "Female, DTC (DECISION)",     109
)

cmp_typ <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_typ,
  reference = table1,
  by = "treatment",
  params = "auclast",
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 5
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp_typ,
  caption = "Typical steady-state AUC0-12 for 400 mg twice daily vs Grevel 2019 Table 1. * differs by more than 5%."
)
```

Each AUC is within 1 percent of Table 1. The small residual reflects the
rounding of CL/F to 9.4 L/h in Table S3; the Table 1 AUCs imply 400 / 42.4 =
9.43 L/h. Because the comparison solves the typical model against its own
clearance, a tight bound is asserted, together with the closed form
AUC0-12,ss = F x Dose / CL. (The female DECISION arm, with a half-life of
about 105 h, is still 0.4 percent short of steady state on day 35.)

```{r typical-assert}
typ_auc <- as.data.frame(nca_typ) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::left_join(table1, by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::left_join(arms, by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    cl_typ = 9.4 * (1 - 0.211 * SEXF) * (1 - 0.506 * STUDY_DECISION),
    closed_form = 400 / cl_typ,
    pct_table1 = 100 * (PPORRES / auclast - 1),
    pct_closed = 100 * (PPORRES / closed_form - 1)
  )

typ_auc |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, cl_typ, closed_form, PPORRES, pct_closed) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Arm" = treatment,
    "Typical CL/F (L/h)" = cl_typ,
    "F x Dose / CL (mg h/L)" = closed_form,
    "PKNCA AUC0-12 (mg h/L)" = PPORRES,
    "% diff" = pct_closed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical CL/F (Table 1 reports 9.4, 7.5, 4.7 and 3.7 L/h) and closed-form AUC check.")

stopifnot(
  all(abs(typ_auc$pct_table1) < 2),
  all(abs(typ_auc$pct_closed) < 1)
)
```

# Simulated steady-state exposure with between-subject variability

```{r stochastic}
n_per_arm <- 100L
ev_sto <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms)), function(i) {
  make_events(
    arms[i, ],
    ids = (i - 1L) * n_per_arm + seq_len(n_per_arm),
    amt = 400,
    dose_times = dose_times,
    obs_times = seq(t_last, t_last + tau, by = 0.25)
  )
}))
sim_sto <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_sto, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()
```

```{r fig-ss-profile}
# Simulated steady-state profiles over one dosing interval, the time window of
# the pc-VPC in Grevel 2019 Figure S3 (which pools all studies and therefore
# cannot be overlaid arm by arm).
sim_sto |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - t_last) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    q05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), q50 = median(Cc), q95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, q50, colour = treatment, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = q05, ymax = q95), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose at steady state (h)",
    y = "Sorafenib plasma concentration (mg/L)",
    colour = NULL, fill = NULL,
    caption = "Median and 90% interval; 400 mg twice daily, day 35. Compare Grevel 2019 Figure S3."
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r pknca-stochastic}
nca_sto <- run_ss_nca(sim_sto, ev_sto, start = t_last, tau = tau)

nca_sto_summary <- as.data.frame(nca_sto) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("auclast", "cmax", "cmin")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median = median(PPORRES),
    p05 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.05),
    p95 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
nca_sto_summary |>
  dplyr::rename("Arm" = treatment, "Parameter" = PPTESTCD, "Median" = median, "5th pct" = p05, "95th pct" = p95) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Steady-state NCA (400 mg twice daily) across 100 virtual subjects per arm.")

auc_med <- nca_sto_summary |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, median) |>
  tibble::deframe()
ratio_dtc <- auc_med[["Male, DTC (DECISION)"]] / auc_med[["Male, HCC/RCC"]]
ratio_dtc
```

The median AUC0-12 in DECISION is about twice that in the HCC/RCC studies,
the "approximate twofold increase in sorafenib exposure in patients with DTC"
of the Results (Table 1: 103 percent). The ratio of medians is checked against
the typical ratio 1 / (1 - 0.506) = 2.02 with a margin for the sampling noise
of two 100-subject medians.

```{r stochastic-assert}
stopifnot(abs(ratio_dtc / (1 / (1 - 0.506)) - 1) < 0.25)
```

# Single dose in the phase I studies

The phase I healthy-volunteer studies were dosed once and have a relative
bioavailability of 1.9 against the steady-state patient studies. The figure
shows the typical profile after a single 400 mg dose with and without that
factor.

```{r single-dose}
arms_sd <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,                         ~SEXF, ~STUDY_DECISION, ~STUDY_SORAFENIB_PHASE1, ~SAMPLE_INTENSIVE,
  "Phase I healthy volunteer (F1 = 1.9)",  0L,              0L,                      1L,                1L,
  "Patient reference (F1 = 1)",            0L,              0L,                      0L,                1L
)
ev_sd <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(arms_sd)), function(i) {
  make_events(arms_sd[i, ], ids = i, amt = 400, dose_times = 0, obs_times = seq(0, 168, by = 0.5))
}))
sim_sd <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_sd, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()

ggplot(sim_sd, aes(time, Cc, colour = treatment)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after a single 400 mg dose (h)",
    y = "Sorafenib plasma concentration (mg/L)",
    colour = NULL,
    caption = "Typical male subject, non-DECISION clearance."
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Exposure under the simulated dosing regimens

Grevel 2019 simulated progression-free survival and adverse events for
continuous dosing at 800, 600 (400 mg am / 200 mg pm) and 400 mg/day in the
DTC population (Figures 2 and 5) and for four dose-reduction schemes starting
with two 28-day cycles at 800 mg/day (Figure 3, Figure S7). The hazard models
that turn those regimens into event rates are not published (see below), but
the PK model gives the exposure each regimen produces. The table shows the
typical steady-state daily AUC in a male DECISION patient; AUC scales with the
daily dose because elimination is linear.

```{r regimens}
regimens <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment,     ~am, ~pm,
  "800 mg/day",   400, 400,
  "600 mg/day",   400, 200,
  "400 mg/day",   200, 200
)
ev_reg <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(regimens)), function(i) {
  amts <- rep(c(regimens$am[i], regimens$pm[i]), length.out = n_doses)
  ev_d <- data.frame(id = i, time = dose_times, amt = amts, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot")
  ev_o <- data.frame(
    id = i, time = seq(t_last - tau, t_last + tau, by = 0.1),
    amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central"
  )
  ev <- dplyr::bind_rows(ev_d, ev_o) |> dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
  ev$SEXF <- 0L
  ev$STUDY_DECISION <- 1L
  ev$STUDY_SORAFENIB_PHASE1 <- 0L
  ev$SAMPLE_INTENSIVE <- 0L
  ev$treatment <- regimens$treatment[i]
  ev
}))
sim_reg <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ, events = ev_reg, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()

nca_reg <- run_ss_nca(sim_reg, ev_reg, start = t_last - tau, tau = 2 * tau)
reg_auc <- as.data.frame(nca_reg) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  dplyr::left_join(regimens, by = "treatment") |>
  dplyr::mutate(closed_form = (am + pm) / (9.4 * (1 - 0.506)))
reg_auc |>
  dplyr::select(treatment, PPORRES, closed_form) |>
  dplyr::rename("Regimen" = treatment, "AUC0-24,ss (mg h/L)" = PPORRES, "Daily dose / CL (mg h/L)" = closed_form) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Typical steady-state AUC over 24 h in a male DECISION patient.")
stopifnot(all(abs(reg_auc$PPORRES / reg_auc$closed_form - 1) < 0.01))
```

# Time-to-event models (not included)

Table 2 of Grevel 2019 lists the hazard models fitted to DECISION: Weibull
with AUC12AV for centrally assessed tumour progression; constant + Gompertz
with average dose for grade 3 or higher adverse events and for grade 3
hand-foot skin reactions; Gompertz with no exposure covariate for grade 4 or
higher adverse events; Weibull with dose rate for grade 2 or higher diarrhoea;
and a constant hazard with AUC12AV for grade 3 or higher hypertension. The
exposure metrics are defined in Equations 1-4 (cycle-wise AUC12, the average
AUC12 up to the event, average dose and dose rate). Neither the article nor
its ten supplementary files report the hazard parameter estimates or the
functional form of the exposure effects, so these models cannot be
reproduced, and the Kaplan-Meier simulations of Figures 2, 3 and 5 are not
replicated here. Back-calculating hazard parameters from the published
Kaplan-Meier bands was not attempted: it would be a fit to digitised
simulations, not the published model.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Covariate effects from Table 1.** Table S3 prints theta8 = -0.2 and
  theta9 = -0.5 to one decimal. The model uses -0.211 and -0.506, the
  percentage differences in CL/F the paper reports in Table 1, which follow
  directly from the linear covariate form of Figure S2 and reproduce the
  Table 1 AUCs to within 1 percent. Table 1 prints the female CL/F in the
  HCC/RCC studies as 7.5 L/h, which matches theta8 = -0.2 (9.4 x 0.8 = 7.52)
  but not its own -21.1 percent row or its AUC of 53.7 mg h/L (400 / 53.7 =
  7.45 L/h); the model gives 7.42 L/h.
- **Other values as printed in Table S3**, mostly to one decimal: CL/F 9.4 L/h,
  ktr 1.0 1/h, F1 1.9, IIV variances 0.2 and 0.4, proportional SDs 0.3 and 0.5.
  The rounding of the variances is coarse (0.2 is 47 percent CV, but anything
  from 0.15 to 0.25 rounds to it).
- **IIV on V1/F retained.** The Methods state that between-patient variability
  of V and ka "could not be estimated reliably", but Table S3 reports an
  estimated IIV on V1 (0.4, 95% CI 0.2-0.7) and Figure S2 includes it, so the
  model follows the table and the equation.
- **Residual-error switch.** Figure S2 uses SD theta4 on occasions with several
  observations and theta6 on occasions with a single observation. This is
  carried by `SAMPLE_INTENSIVE` (1 = several samples on the occasion); the
  additive component (theta5) was fixed to 0 and is omitted.
- **Study indicators.** The DECISION effect is keyed on the study number in
  Figure S2 and is encoded as `STUDY_DECISION`; the paper states it cannot be
  separated from an effect of the DTC indication. The single-dose
  bioavailability is encoded as `STUDY_SORAFENIB_PHASE1`, which in this pool
  coincides with the healthy-volunteer and single-dose records. To simulate a
  new non-DECISION population, set `STUDY_DECISION = 0`.
- **Enterohepatic recirculation.** The multiple peaks seen in the dense phase I
  profiles are not modelled; the three-transit absorption chain stands in for
  them (Discussion). For a model with explicit recirculation see
  `Jain_2011_sorafenib`.
- **Time-to-event models omitted** for lack of published estimates (previous
  section).
